newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-China bankers say autonomous Hong Kong vital.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-China bankers say autonomous Hong Kong vital.

text.p: Two of China's most powerful bankers on Tuesday said it was crucial that Hong Kong kept its freedom to operate as a major international financial centre when it comes under Beijing rule next year.
"It is...vital that Hong Kong remain the vibrant financial centre with its own economic system that we know now," the deputy governor of the People's Bank of China, Chen Yuan said.
Beijing needed Hong Kong to remain an independent financial centre to help China's own economic development once it regains control of the territory from Britain on July 1 next year.
"We certainly would not do anything which would jeopardise Hong Kong's prospects," Chen told a Bank of England seminar.
China would even use its own currency reserves to defend the Hong Kong dollar and its 13-year old peg to the U.S. currency.
"We...stand ready to use our foreign reserves to support the Hong Kong dollar if necessary...The People's Bank of China will support the currency stability of Hong Kong," he said.

Chen dismissed suggestions that Beijing would not honour its agreements after it takes over and he ruled out the chances of a booming Shanghai taking over Hong Kong's role, arguing that China was big enough to have more than one financial centre.

"We firmly believe that prospects for Hong Kong's economy and finance will be glorious and magnificent," Wang Xue Bing, chairman of the country's leading commercial bank the Bank of China, told the seminar.
He denied his bank had any intention of trying to use its influence to dominate Hong Kong's financial sector.
"We deeply realise that a stable and prosperous operating environment is an essential guarantee for the existence and development of the financial industry," he said.
Western bankers and the head of Hong Kong's own Monetary Authority were equally enthusiastic about British colony's prospects under Chinese rule.

"Notwithstanding the high degree of monetary authority Hong Kong has been enjoying, there will in fact be an even higher degree of monetary autonomy...as a result of the transfer of sovereignty," the head of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA), Joseph Yam, said.
He described as myths any fears that once China took over there would be massive capital flight, that the Hong Kong dollar would disappear or the exchange rate link would be abandoned.
"The playing field will not be tilted in favour of Mainland interests after 1997," Lam said.

"The transition to Chinese sovereignty is part of a broader transition, a broader dynamic, that will lead Hong Kong successfully into the next century," said William Purves, chairman of HSBC Holdings Plc, one of the three banknote issuing banks in Hong Kong.
His counterpart at Standard Chartered Bank Plc, Patrick Gillam, said there may be political tension over the local legislature but was confident the transition would work.
"China is entering a period of controlled growth and Hong Kong is as prosperous as ever...so you have all the right circumstances in place," Gillam said.
Bank of England Governor Eddie George underscored the need for an uneventful change of power.
"It is in the interest of all of us...that the transition should proceed smoothly and that the special characteristics of Hong Kong Kong be preserved into the future," George said.
